question.text: This modern-day Balkan country staged a decades-long revolt against Ottoman rule in the 15th century led by Skanderbeg. In the 20th century, it was ruled by the dictator Enver Hoxha (HOE-juh).
question.clue: This nation was flooded with refugees from the nearby Kosovo War, and joined NATO in 2009.

swap.leadin: Its source is in the Black Forest region of Germany.
swap.text: Name this river that flows through Vienna long before it reaches the Black Sea.
swap.clue: Wooden arches and twenty masonry pillars were used as the base of a massive bridge built over this river by Apollodorus of Damascus just east of a gorge known as the Iron Gates.

question.leadin: A country is not actually a country until the United Nations officially recognizes it. Identify these "wannabe" nations.
question.text: With its capital at Pristina and a population of mostly Albanians, it declared independence from Serbia in 2008, but Russia blocked its recognition with a veto.
question.clue: This country was the location of a battle where Ottoman Sultan Murad I was killed, while a war named for this modern day nation involved Operation Noble Anvil and was waged largely by the KLA.

swap.text: This former Yugoslav President was tried for war crimes at The Hague, but died in prison in of a heart attack in 2006 while still awaiting a verdict.
swap.clue: He was overthrown in the 2000 Bulldozer Revolution.

question.text: Ferdinand and his wife Sophie were assassinated by this Yugoslav nationalist who was associated with the Young Bosnia movement.
question.clue: The failure of Nedeljko Cabrinovic ] to complete a task with a hand grenade prompted this member of Young Bosnia to carry out his most infamous action, after which he exclaimed "I am a Yugoslav nationalist" during trial.

swap.leadin: The destroyed Vukovar Water Tower was preserved to commemorate massacres against this country's people.
swap.text: Name this country which was led in its war of independence by Franjo Tudjman. Separatists in this country led the Log Revolution and bombarded the medieval Old Town of Dubrovnik.
swap.clue: This country was merged with Slavonia in 1868, though Rijeka ] remained separate.

question.leadin: This man formed the Non-Aligned Movement with Nasser and Nehru.
question.text: Identify this man who led his country to become the only member of Cominform to repel Soviet domination.
question.clue: Political opponents of this leader were sent to the prison island of Goli Otok during the Informbiro period.

swap.leadin: In this leader's last public appearance, people shouted "Timisoara" in reference to an uprising he had violently suppressed.
swap.text: Name this long-time Communist leader of Romania. This man and his wife's execution was nearly caught on live television following a 1989 revolution.
swap.clue: In an effort to increase his country's population, he outlawed almost all forms ofcontraception in Decree 770, and he employed a secret police known as the Securitate.

question.leadin: The early rulers of these people, including Asparukh, are listed in the Nominalia.
question.text: Name these people who were soundly defeated at the Battle of Kleidion by Basil II, who was nicknamed the "Slayer" of these people.
question.clue: The emperor Nikephoros I had his skull turned into a silver cup after he was killed by some of these people at the battle of Pliska, at which their leader was Krum.

swap.leadin: The army of the losing nation in the first of these conflicts was able to make a stand at Chataldzha and save its capital.
swap.text: Identify this series of conflicts, the second of which began over border disputes in Macedonia.
swap.clue: The first of these was ended by the Treaty of London, though it left the possession of Salonika and Thrace unresolved.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a 1204 swerve that really surprised Byzantine-era observers.
question.text: An early event in the Fourth Crusade featured crusaders attacking this rival of Venice in November 1202. Pope Innocent III pointed out this city was a Catholic city and excommunicated the crusaders for going rogue.

swap.leadin: Identify these allies of Adolf Hitler.
swap.text: This Romanian dictator, who came to power in 1940 by forcing the abdication of King Carol, established the National Legionary State, which shipped thousands of his own people to Nazi death camps. He was executed by the Communist regime.
swap.clue: This leader's army launched Operation Munchen to reclaim Bessarabia and Northern Bukovina, and massacred Jews in Odessa and Iasi.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the hit Serbian propaganda song "God is a Serb," sometimes erroneously called "Serbia Strong."
question.text: "God is a Serb" refers to Croats as members of this fascist organization. Founded by Ante Pavelic, it collaborated with German and Italian occupiers and nominally ruled Croatia during World War II.
question.clue: Along with the Nazi party, the Bigelow Report outed the Roman Catholic church for hiding this organization's gold.

swap.text: Kun's rise to power occurred during a conflict with this country, the eastern neighbor of Hungary, which incorporated Transylvania and parts of Banat after the Treaty of Trianon.
swap.clue: Gaining independence after the Russo-Turkish War of 1878 under King Carol I, this country saw one long-time ruler begin a small cultural revolution with the July Theses and establish a police force called the Securitate.

question.leadin: Name the following 20th century eastern European leaders.
question.text: This patron of Nicolae Ceausescu was the Communist leader of Romania from 1948 to 1965. Domestically, he emphasized the manufacturing of consumer goods, while he sought to improve foreign relations with both the West and China.
question.clue: Together with Petru Groza, this Romanian leader reportedly held King Michael at gunpoint to convince him to abdicate. After becoming prime minister in 1952, he forged alliances with China and other non-communist states, before being succeeded as party leader by Nicolae Ceausescu ("chow-SHES-koo").

swap.leadin: As part of a movement against the Phanariotes ("fuh-NAH-ree-its"), Pandur ("PAHN-doo'r") irregulars in this region under Tudor Vladimirescu ("vlah-dee-mee-RESS-koo") led an 1821 uprising as an implicit attack against Ottoman rule.
swap.text: Name this region, which in the 19th century formed the United Principalities with the nearby region of Moldavia.
swap.clue: This region was the first one to be ruled by Michael the Brave.

question.leadin: This man helped put down a peasant revolt in Galati in 1907, and once in power executed high level dignitaries at Jilava Prison.
question.text: Identify this prime minister under King Carol II who allied his country with the Nazis during World War II.

swap.leadin: Many of these institutions in Guatemala were closed after a fire at one called Hogar Seguro left 41 people dead.
swap.text: Name these institutions. In the early 1990s, the 20/20 program "Shame of a Nation" called attention to the horrible state of these institutions in Romania.
swap.answerHtml: orphanages [or children’s homes; prompt on care homes; reject “foster homes”]
swap.clue: This type of institution run by the Salzburger emigrants. Dissatisfied with the standards of institutions of this type, Charles Loring Brace operated a controversial "Train Movement" to supplant them.

question.leadin: After this man was diagnosed with polycythemia, he joked that he was "suffering from an excess of reds."
question.text: What Archbishop was controversially put on trial by Tito and convicted for treason for his relationship with the Ustase government during World War II? While eventually released from prison, he died soon after and was declared a martyr years later by Pope John Paul II.

swap.text: Tuđman launched Operation Storm and obliterated the forces of Serbian Krajina after agreeing to lend this leader military aid via the Split Agreement. With Tuđman and Slobodon Milosevic, this first President of Bosnia and Herzegovina signed the 1995 Dayton Accords.
